These appeals are filed by the petitioner/claimant as well as the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 29.02.2020 passed in MVC No. 458 of 2018 by the Court of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Jamkhandi.

sentences.text:
Brief facts leading rise to the filing of these appeals are as follows:
2.1.
On 03.12.2017, the petitioner met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-20/Z-4843, as the car had hit a tree.
The petitioner was an inmate of the car and has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
It is contended that, he was working as a Mason and was earning 600/- per day; due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, he is unable to do any work.
Hence, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking a compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
2.2. Respondent No.1/owner of the car filed the statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and admitted the ownership of the car.
It is contended that, car was insured by respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
The driver of the car held a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident.
Hence, the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify respondent No.1-the owner.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the claim petition against respondent No.1-owner of the car.

2.3. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition, and contended that the driver of the car did not possess a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident.

There is a violation of policy conditions and hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR 2.4.
The Tribunal, based on the pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.

Sajjanand @ Shajanand vs Sri Hanamanth S/O. Lakshman Wajentri on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14762152/
3 2.5.
The petitioner, to substantiate the claim petition, examined his mother as PW1, examined the Doctor as CW1 and marked 181 documents as Exs.P1 to P181, and 6 documents were marked as Exs.C1 to C6.

In rebuttal, the Insurance Company examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and marked 2 documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
2.6.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs vide judgment dated 29.02.2020and awarded a compensation of 20,62,095/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation and the Insurance Company was directed to deposit the compensation amount along with accrued interest.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR 3.

The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
filed the appeal in MFA No. 100781 of 2021 and the Insurance Company, aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, preferred the appeal in MFA No. 100349 of 2021.

4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner was working as a Mason and he was aged about 23 years as of the date of accident.
He was earning 600/- per day.

He submits that,
the petitioner has examined the Doctor as CW1 who has opined that the petitioner has suffered brain impairment of 97% and the Tribunal has assessed 100% disability to the whole body, which is just and proper.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income at 8,000/- which is on the lower side.

He submits that, in the absence of income proof, the Tribunal NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR could have assessed the notional income as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority ('KSLSA' for short).
The accident is of 2017.
The notional income has to be assessed at 10,250/- with 40% future prospects i.e., 14,350/-.
He submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on the lower side.

Hence, on these grounds,
he prays to allow the appeal filed by the petitioner and to dismiss the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.
6. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is exorbitant.
He submits that, though the Doctor has opined that the petitioner has suffered 97% disability, the Tribunal has taken the disability at 100% which is on the higher side.
Hence, on these grounds, prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioner and to allow the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR 7.
Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
8. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.

4 9.

It is undisputed that the petitioner was proceeding as an inmate in the offending car and the driver of the offending car drove the car in rash and negligent manner, he lost control over the car and dashed to a tree.
As a result, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The petitioner, to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car, has produced the charge sheet marked as Ex.P6.
The Tribunal was justified in recording its finding that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Reg. 
Quantum of compensation:
10.
It is undisputed that the petitioner was aged about 23 years as of the date of accident.
The petitioner NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR contended that he was working as a Mason and used to earn 600/- per day.
To substantiate his claim, the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, this Court reassesses the notional income at 10,350/- as per the schedule issued by the KSLSA, as the accident is of 2017.

Further, 40% future prospects is to be added to the notional income of 10,250/-, which comes to 14,350/- as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1.

awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of 15,21,000/-.
For the foregoing, the point is answered accordingly.

12. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
MFA No. 100781 of 2021 is partly allowed; ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is hereby modified;
iii. The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of 35,83,095/-, as against 20,62,095/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced - 12 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3582 HC-KAR compensation of 15,21,000/- with 6% interest per annum from the date of the petition till its realization;
iv.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment; v. MFA No. 100349 of 2021 is dismissed; vi.
